findings.title: Your website does not load securely
findings.why: Browsers mark a site without HTTPS as not secure, and anything a patient types into it, like a name or phone number, travels without encryption. That is the first thing a cautious patient notices.
findings.fix: Ask your web host to turn on a free HTTPS certificate and send every visit to the https:// address.

findings.title: Plain HTTP visits are not moved to HTTPS
findings.why: Anyone who types your address without https, or follows an old link, gets an unencrypted page. On public Wi-Fi in a waiting room, that page can be read or changed in transit.
findings.fix: Set your site or host to permanently redirect every http:// request to https://.

findings.title: Some browser security settings are missing
findings.why: Security headers tell a visitor's browser how to protect your pages, for example to refuse being framed inside a fake site or to always use HTTPS. Without them, your site leans on the browser's weakest defaults.
findings.fix: Ask your web developer or host to add the missing headers listed above; most hosts can set them in one place.

findings.title: A form on your homepage is not encrypted
findings.why: Your homepage loads over plain HTTP, so whatever a patient types into its form, such as a name, phone number or reason for visit, travels unencrypted. The HIPAA Security Rule asks practices to protect patient information in transit.
findings.fix: Turn on HTTPS for the whole site and redirect every http:// visit to https://.

findings.title: A form or booking frame sends information without encryption
findings.why: The page is secure, but the form or embedded booking tool sends what patients type to a plain http:// address. Browsers may block it outright or warn the patient, and the information is not protected on the way.
findings.fix: Change the form or booking embed to its https:// address; your booking vendor can confirm the right link.
